title: (No AI) OpenAI announces three big science discoveries and a new way to work with academics
author: Richard Lawler
content:
![OpenAI logo with a background of complex math formulas.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/STKS537_AI_MATH_2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Less than a month after its [mass release of hundreds of manuscripts](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1008726/openai-mathematics-solutions-chaos) that it said contained solutions to long-standing mathematics questions, OpenAI is back with [three more "major" discoveries in math, computer science, and physics](https://openai.com/index/building-scientific-understanding-with-academic-communities/). title: (No AI) Anthropic is burning gas to feed the AI boom
author: Justine Calma
content:
![Anthropic logo on an orange and gray background.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/01/STK269_ANTHROPIC_2_B.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

As it [prepares to go public](https://www.anthropic.com/news/s1-sec), Anthropic's [S-1 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026067168/anthropicpbc-sx1.htm) makes generative AI's methane dependency glaringly obvious.

> "Competition for access to electrical supply and data center locations with adequate power availability is intense."

In documents filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission Monday, Anthropic acknowledges that data centers are becoming increasingly reliant on "natural gas" - the fossil fuel industry's [marketing term](https://www.vox.com/22912760/natural-gas-methane-rename) for what is primarily methane - leaving the company's AI data center buildout vulnerable to rising fuel costs and existing supply chain constraints.
